summary: Roche reports one positive and one failed TED pivotal trial. The prior Astra review describes weak SatraGO-1 mean-proptosis results and descriptive secondary analyses, leaving efficacy sufficiency and label scope unresolved.
pivotalQuestion: Does the totality of prespecified evidence establish clinically meaningful TED benefit for the proposed population despite SatraGO-1’s primary failure and weak mean-proptosis results?

factors.rationale: Roche reports SatraGO-2 met the primary endpoint; SatraGO-1 missed. The prior Astra review notes anti-inflammatory activity in both, but weak SatraGO-1 mean-proptosis results and only descriptive secondary analyses.
The prior Astra review reports similar Week 24 serious-event counts and no deaths, but more ALT elevations and neutrophil decreases in SatraGO-2; severity and longer-term safety remain unresolved.

The prior Astra review identifies an earlier CMC supplement approval, but no manufacturing assessment linked to the TED application. That earlier action does not establish clearance for this supplement.

Roche reports priority sBLA acceptance and an October 15 review target; July’s update retains the filing. Neither acceptance nor prior NMOSD approval establishes TED efficacy or FDA agreement on label scope.
